The handoff refs are B.txt and D.txt. Under the stated convention, the preferred pair is the two letters outside them, A (radon/raw.py) and C (radon/metrics.py). They get 41 of the 60 minutes. I did not open the handoff_refs files or read raw.py or metrics.py, so the decoding rests on the convention as you described it.

The sorting logic itself is in radon/complexity.py (B):
- radon/complexity.py:10-12 defines the three keys. SCORE is `lambda block: -GET_COMPLEXITY(block)`, LINES is `block.lineno`, and ALPHA is `block.name`.
- radon/complexity.py:59-75 defines `sorted_results(blocks, order=SCORE)`, which returns `sorted(blocks, key=order)`. SCORE is descending because of the negation, and it is the default.

B therefore holds the code the request is about, but the decoded pair is where most of the time goes. Within A and C, the review should check whether their measured blocks expose `lineno`, `name` and a complexity value that these key functions can use. B gets 15 minutes to cover the keys and the sort call, and D gets 4 minutes as a quick check.

A is the primary file only because it is first in the decoded pair. The most concrete evidence is in B.
